items.title: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI
items.raw_text: Research acceleration: The view inside OpenAI Apparently today is RSI day at OpenAI, for Recursive Self-Improvement - I think it's their new AGI. Both this piece and the new essay An Alien Mind (by Chief Scientist Jakub Pachocki) talk about it, and this one doesn't even bother to expand the acronym. Included are details on how OpenAI's own research team are using coding agents. Like pretty much everyone else 2026 has been the year that agentic engineering really took off at OpenAI, best illustrated by this chart: I'm intrigued at what caused that significant acceleration in AI spend per researcher in late July - my best guess is that's when internal employees gained access to the model later released as GPT-6 Astra. items.title: Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries (New Journal Article)
items.raw_text: The article linked below was published by Public Library Quarterly. Title Accountability, Integrity: AI Policy in Public Libraries Authors Kathryn FitzGerald University of Washington Benjamin Lee University of Washington Source Public Library Quarterly DOI: 1 0.1080/01616846.2026.2725502 Abstract As artificial intelligence reshapes both library work and the information environment, public libraries must determine whether or how to engage with AI while maintaining library values. To our knowledge, there exists no published analysis of how American and Canadian public library AI policies might link library values and technology adoption. To address this gap, we conducted an environmental scan of public library websites to identify and analyze AI policy statements. Our scan of over 200 library websites identified 32 AI polcies. All reference at least two values, with privacy, security, and responsibility the most frequently cited. items.title: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams
items.raw_text: The purpose of DNS is to spread scams Terence Eden shares some daunting statistics in support of his take that "the Domain Name System's purpose seems to be a vector for criminals to run scams on people at a terrifyingly high rate". On this Interisle report ( via Andrew Campling ), Terence says: It says 85 million new registrations of gTLDs were made in 2025. Of those 8.5 million were added to blocklists by May 2025. It reckons that a 10% abuse rate is the likely floor for these numbers and it's probably closer to 20%. One in five newly registered domains with a gTLD are scams. That's a bloody crisis. I had no idea. Apparently ICANN have been discussing this problem for years. Tags: dns , scams , terence-eden

items.title: There's No Limit to How Bad Code Can Get
items.raw_text: My comment on There's No Limit to How Bad Code Can Get — Lobste.rs. [In reply to a comment about burning it down to start from scratch when technical debt becomes overwhelming] In my experience it's so rare for that to work. You announce the old thing is irrecoverably drowning in tech debt. You spin up a team to rewrite it from scratch. Work begins. Meanwhile the old thing remains a moving target: it's running the core business, so changes are still necessary. The developers working on it know that it's going to be made obsolete by the new thing soon, so they don't have any incentive to go beyond the smallest effort possible to add the new features. Technical debt continues to mount. Meanwhile, the team working on the new thing are ambitious and probably a little naive. They start out at a great pace - it's greenfield after all - but as time progresses it becomes apparent that nobody fully understands the behavior and scope of the thing they are replacing. If it was well documented and tested it wouldn't need to be replaced, after all... After months (or even years) without delivering value, the pressure is on to "ship it", so the new system is launched to handle a subset of what the old system handled - or often for some new feature that was too hard to build with the now mostly unmaintained old system. ... so now you have TWO systems in production - the janky old system that nobody wants to touch, and a new system which handles just a few production features and is 80% inac

items.title: Report: The Federal Program Keeping Libraries Online? the FCC Might Gut It
items.raw_text: From the Indianapolis Star: Under the atrium at the Indianapolis Public Library , a woman is busily typing away on her laptop. Another patron seated at the Central Branch is charging their device while streaming music through earbuds as they read quietly between the stacks. Free Wi-Fi allows Hoosiers a cozy and safe place to access the internet at all 26 library locations across Indianapolis. Potential cuts, however, by the Federal Communications Commission have put that access at risk, advocates warn, and not just in Indiana, but for millions of people in libraries and public schools across the country. The FCC recently put into question whether a 30-year-old program that helps keep libraries online should be changed, left alone, or end. No decisions have been reached, but librarians are concerned about what it could mean for their funding. In late June, the FCC issued what appeared to be a benign notice addressing child safety under one of its service operations. Buried within the 86-page document were eight words that sent shockwaves among librarians and educators alike: “Should the E-Rate program be limited or sunset?” [Clip] “This definitely caught us by surprise,” said Jamar Rahming , president-elect of the Public Library Association and CEO of Cuyahoga County Public Library in Cleveland, Ohio. “E-Rate has been just such a fixture in our public library institutions and communities.” Learn More, Read the Complete Article (about 2300 words) The post Report: The Federal Pr

items.title: Report: “DC Librarian Offers Paid Internship to Boost Interest in Library Science”
items.raw_text: From WTOP: In 2019, Christopher Stewart started paying students in D.C. to work in a school library and learn about the field. The concept is similar to a paid internship, with students helping with research and shelving books. The goal is to increase students’ awareness of library science and spark their interest in the field. Stewart has brought the program with him to various schools. Now in his first year as senior school librarian at Garnet-Patterson S.T.A.Y. High School, Stewart has opened applications for hiring two library brand ambassadors. He’s already received information from six applicants. The mission, he said, is to “make sure that students have an opportunity to explore the field, particularly Black and Brown students, because we make up so little as far as the grand total of librarians, especially school librarians.” Learn More, Read the Complete Article The post Report: “DC Librarian Offers Paid Internship to Boost Interest in Library Science” appeared first on Library Journal infoDOCKET .

items.raw_text: The below message has been distributed to IFLA members and volunteers in all IFLA languages. I will admit that I lost count of the number of meetings, speeches and other events I was involved in, but know that each one reinforced my excitement about libraries and our Federation. I will also admit to some pride in my gong technique. I want to begin by highlight the incredible winners of our awards this year, as well as our IFLA Medal and Scroll of Appreciation recipients. Thank you for all you do in support of libraries, our profession and IFLA. It was inspiring to see the extent to which political decision-makers in Korea both understand the potential of libraries and support libraries in realizing their potential. It is a situation we can all aspire to! It was such a pleasure to have an opportunity to talk individually with so many of you attending the Congress, whether members, volunteers or stakeholders, to thank you for your incredible support and friendship. I am sorry that I couldn’t connect personally with everyone, but I do hope that you are already putting our Congress next year in London in your diaries. items.title: Association of American Publishers (AAP) and The Authors Guild Release New Study Analyzing the Impact of Library E-Lending on Commercial Book Markets
items.raw_text: From a Joint Release: Today, the Association of American Publishers (AAP) and the Authors Guild announced the release of a landmark independent study by leading economists at Secretariat Advisors, titled An Empirical Study of the Impact of Library E-Lending on the Book Economy. The study, commissioned jointly by AAP and the Authors Guild, but independently conducted by Secretariat Advisors’ economists, provides the most rigorous analysis to date of how the steep shift toward digital lending in recent years has affected the commercial marketplace for books in the United States, specifically, the consumer sales on which authors and publishers rely for financial success. The research concludes that increased digital access to e-books through library apps influences consumer behavior and impacts commercial markets across both physical and digital formats. The study further concludes there is robust and economically meaningful evidence of direct substitution between library e-lending and retail sales and that decreases in library e-book prices or certain other changes to licensing terms, as required in recent state legislative initiatives, would cause further harm to commercial markets. Authors, publishers, and libraries enjoy a close relationship and shared objective to promote and maximize reading across all levels of society, not only to champion established works of literature but to support the continued production of books not yet written. items.title: The Great IFLA100 Futures Challenge
items.raw_text: Join us on the first stage of our drive to engage the global library field in a reflection on the future(s) of our institutions, our place in society, and our international cooperation. A key pillar of the programme for IFLA’s centenary year – IFLA100 – is a focus on the future. Alongside the remembering and celebration of our past achievements and the people that made them possible, we want this year to be a chance to build up the skills, attitudes and connections necessary to enter into our second century with confidence. Central to this is our work to build up the habit of futures thinking across our profession. This enables us to steer a path between a denialism driven by passivity, and an excessive reliance on specific predictions that leaves little room to react to the unexpected. IFLA already has a strong record of work in this space. Our Trend Report in 2024 shared a set of potential trends, as well as using these to offer a range of potential scenarios for the future, ready to be used by libraries and library workers to test their own plans. Our Weak Signals report added to this, using ideas gathered at the 2025 World Library and Information Congress to identify phenomena that could potentially have a transformative effect in the future. At our 2026 Congress, the keynote speech by Sohail Inayatullah provided further insights into techniques for futures thinking, complementing the keynote given by Riel Miller at our Toronto meetings in April. items.title: “A Secure Environment to Explore”: Learn About the AI Sandbox Initiative For Staff at the Library of Congress
items.raw_text: From an LC Blog Post: In 2025, the Library introduced its AI Sandbox for staff initiative to do just that. “Sandbox” environments have been used since the early 1970s to provide protected spaces for development and experimentation without risk to systems. [Clip] While AI technologies have growing potential to augment and enrich the Library’s collections and services, experimentation and security are key. To better understand how these creative and innovative methods might work with various materials and conditions, the most recent cohort of the Library’s AI Sandbox for staff supported over a dozen small-scale experiments. Teams incorporated technical and subject matter expertise to focus their experimentation on the real-life demands and possibilities for Library workflows. [Clip] Projects focused on materials spanning the Library’s rich collections: legal records and briefs; circulars and regulations; images; talking books; audiovisual materials, classified ads from historic newspapers; web archived government PDFs; manuscript materials in Arabic, Persian, Ge’ez, Turkish, Armenian, Georgian, Japanese, Chinese, and Hebrew; children’s and young adult books, sound recordings; web archived metadata; record annotations; oral history recordings; non-Latin monographs; catalog records; training materials and resources; and even more items accessible via the Library of Congress collections API . items.title: Call for Proposals: Consultancy on International Association Membership, Volunteer and Congress Models
items.raw_text: IFLA is looking for a consultant that can support work to ensure that our membership, volunteer and Congress financial models are optimised as we enter our second century, drawing on insights and best practice from peer organisations. This work takes place as part of our Sustainable Futures Journey, which brings together a range of initiatives intended to strengthen our Federation’s ability to deliver on its current and future strategies. The work on reviews of our membership, volunteer and congress financial models is being led by members of our Governing Board, with a strong emphasis on engaging our communities and partners, and drawing on their experience and ideas. At the same time, we are realistic about the fact that there are many other international associations which face similar situations to our own, and which can offer us valuable lessons and ideas to inform our own work. This is where we are seeking a consultant who can support the work of our Board by bringing together key examples and inputs. Details of our expectations are set out in the formal call , which is open until 15 September. We welcome applications from around the world, and from teams of consultants.

De nota noemt bijvoorbeeld AI voor het analyseren van dreigingen en het ondersteunen van besluitvorming. Ook wil het ministerie de digitale infrastructuur opschalen, voor onder meer inlichtingen en de grootschalige inzet van drones. Veilige cloudvoorzieningen, cyberverdediging en versleuteling beschermen informatie tegen huidige en nieuwe digitale dreigingen. items.title: Kabinet investeert 102,5 miljoen in MedTech
items.raw_text: De ministeries van VWS en EZK investeren tot en met 2036 samen 102,5 miljoen euro in de Nederlandse MedTech-sector. Private partijen leggen daar minimaal hetzelfde bedrag bij. De ambitie van het kabinet is om in 2035 het sterkste MedTech-ecosysteem van Europa te zijn. De publiek-private investering is een reactie op het Groeiplan MedTech, onderdeel van het rapport Wennink. De afspraken werden op 6 juli aangekondigd tijdens een werkconferentie met twee ministers en twee directeuren-generaal. De overheid ziet het als haar rol om de randvoorwaarden voor AI in de zorg te versterken, zoals passende wet- en regelgeving, zorgimplementatie en data- en AI-infrastructuur. Dit is een greep uit onze activiteiten van de afgelopen maanden. GAI-leidraad en AI Fabriek Onduidelijkheid over wet- en regelgeving remt het gebruik van generatieve AI in de zorg. items.title: Wouter van Balveren van OBGZ over minibiebs: “We hebben eigenlijk 350 vestigingen”
items.raw_text: In Nijmegen staan honderden minibiebs in de stad. De bibliotheek besloot niet te concurreren met deze kleine boekenkastjes die iedereen wel uit het straatbeeld herkent, maar juist te kijken wat ze voor elkaar kunnen betekenen. Wouter van Balveren, innovatiemanager bij OBGZ (Nijmegen en omstreken) vertelt hoe de samenwerking met de minibiebeigenaren ontstond, wat het oplevert en hoe je een samenwerking opzet. Kun je kort vertellen wat jullie met de minibiebs doen? “Minibiebs zijn natuurlijk al heel lang overal te vinden. Wij zagen ze ook om ons heen. Je kunt daar op twee manieren naar kijken. Je kunt het zien als een bedreiging en denken: dat is niet wat wij als bibliotheek zijn. Wij hebben een actuele, zorgvuldig samengestelde collectie. Wat heb je dan aan zo’n minibieb? Maar je kunt het ook anders bekijken. Het zijn enthousiaste mensen die van lezen houden en het leuk vinden om boeken en verhalen met anderen te delen. In die zin zijn het eigenlijk ambassadeurs van leesplezier, net als wij. Daarnaast past het goed bij onze missie: wij staan voor leesplezier, verhalen en toegang tot boeken voor iedereen. items.title: German company becomes first in Europe to launch fully commercial orbital rocket
items.raw_text: Isar Aerospace, founded in 2018 by three students at a German university, successfully launched a privately-developed rocket into low-Earth orbit Saturday from a Norwegian spaceport inside the Arctic Circle. The two-stage rocket, named Spectrum, became the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. With Saturday's success, Isar is the clear leader among a pack of several European launch startups vying to inject some competition into Europe's stagnant launch market. Isar's 92-foot-tall (28-meter) Spectrum rocket lifted off at 4:12 pm EST (20:12 UTC) Saturday from Andøya Spaceport in northern Norway, where it was 10:12 pm local time as the final bluish hues of daylight faded from the late summer sky. Seven minutes later, the rocket was in orbit. Read full article Comments

items.title: Farmed salmon may not be as nutritious as it once was, new research suggests
items.raw_text: Eat more fatty fish. That dietary advice has changed the way the world consumes salmon, pushing consumer demand ever upward and production to higher and higher levels. Most of that demand is being met with farmed salmon: Today, nearly 70 percent of the salmon consumed on the planet are raised in pens and cages. The US Department of Agriculture’s Dietary Guidelines for Americans recommend eating at least 8 ounces of fish a week and urges people to choose salmon or other species that are similarly high in “heart-healthy” Omega-3 fatty acids. But new research led by USDA scientists finds that levels of these fatty acids in farmed salmon have dropped considerably, potentially making the agency’s own advice, and similar recommendations, including from the American Heart Association, outdated and insufficient. items.raw_text: Tesla’s Cybercab, a distinctive two-seater without a steering wheel or brake pedals, is set to start picking up members of the public in two states. But the vehicle is already under investigation by the US federal government, which is probing whether it meets federal safety standards. The investigation comes just hours after the electric automaker welcomed hundreds of fans to downtown Austin to ride in the driverless Cybercabs. Tesla plans to deploy the vehicles on its Robotaxi ride-hail network , which is currently operating in a handful of cities in Texas and Florida. The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration is updating vehicle standards to make it easier and faster for driverless cars to deploy on public roads. It’s currently tweaking eight rules, including those requiring car parts that driverless cars don’t really need: brake pedals, windshield wipers, and rearview mirrors. But for now, years-old standards remain in place. Read full article Comments

items.title: Ask HN: Fable hacked my piano, can I release the results?
items.raw_text: I have a self playing piano, using a system called PianoDisc Protigy. They have an online store which sells music for their system, from various modern artists along with classics such as Bach and Beethoven. Last night I saw they had released some music from Eric Satre, a 19th century French composer, which I bought. Curious if I could have just used AI to create these files, I began experimenting with Astra and Fable. Feeding the output of one into the other to critique. After an hour of LLM discussion of Rubato and fermata, solenoid response times and proper sustain pedal technique, they settled on their ultimate version of Gymnopedie No 1. I then asked Fable to compare it to the open source version I'd downloaded from Mutopia, which it promptly ripped apart. No sustain, zero rubato, upside down balance. Ok, what about the version I'd just bought? The PianoDisc versions are mp3s encoded with the right channel carrying MIDI to be played on the piano, and the left channel containing any accompanying music to be played through attached speakers (who doesn't want the harmonica on Piano Man?) I gave the mp3 to Fable, which promptly decoded the format, identifying the right channel carrying MIDI using a 2004.5 Hz square wave. It then went on to analyze the nuance of pedal lift and melody relative to the chords. Fable then asked if I wanted it to build an encoder to write my own MIDI files into the right channel of mp3s. items.title: Limiting Risk in the Face of Uncertainty
items.raw_text: If you save for retirement when you are young, the standard advice is to emphasize stock-based exchange-traded funds (ETFs) or mutual funds. Stocks increase and decrease in dramatic ways that no one can predict reliably, so this approach carries some risk. Fortunately for US stock market investors, that risk has historically been rewarded, on average and over the long term, with high returns. As you approach retirement and need to rely on investments to cover living expenses, the standard advice is to shift your portfolio toward bond-based ETFs or mutual funds. Bonds have had fewer and less dramatic booms and busts. For this reason, they are generally considered less risky than stocks. On average, over the long term, bonds’ safety has meant lower, more reliable returns than stocks. Risk makes less sense for ALA right now. Because of its financial deficit , the Association needs stability. Therefore, in April, ALA’s Endowment Trustees updated the target allocation for the Association’s investment portfolio, reducing our holdings of stocks from 50% to 40%, and increasing ALA’s holdings of bonds from 30% to 40%. As a result, we are sacrificing some projected returns to limit projected risk. If stocks boom as they have in the past few years, ALA’s portfolio will not increase as much as it would have. items.title: Prentenboeken in Papiamentu: een feest van herkenning
items.raw_text: Een prentenboek vertalen lijkt eenvoudig: je zet de ene taal om in de andere. Maar hoe zorg je ervoor dat een kind zich écht herkent in een verhaal? Waarom is de keuze voor opa beter dan de officiële vertaling tawela? Waarom mocht het verhaal van Tula in de nieuwe prentenboekencollectie niet ontbreken? En wat gebeurt er als een kind voor het eerst een verhaal in zijn eigen taal hoort? Jakeema, Myrthe en Margriet vertellen hoe juist die keuzes het verschil maken. items.title: Bouw je eigen AI-assistent: van losse prompts naar een digitale collega
items.raw_text: Veel mensen gebruiken AI als vraagbaak: je start een chat, stelt een vraag, krijgt antwoord en begint de volgende keer weer met een nieuwe chat. Een AI-assistent oftewel een ‘custom agent’ werkt net anders: het is een digitale collega die je inwerkt op een specifieke taak. De grootste winst? Die ligt in het automatiseren van repeterende werkzaamheden, zodat er meer tijd overblijft voor strategie, creativiteit en contact met jouw doelgroep. In dit artikel lees je wat een AI-assistent is en hoe je er zelf een kunt inrichten om efficiënter te kunnen werken. Wat is een AI-assistent? Een AI-assistent kun je inrichten om een specifieke taak zo goed mogelijk uit te voeren. In plaats van bij iedere nieuwe chat opnieuw uit te leggen wat je wilt, geef je de assistent vooraf context, instructies en relevante documenten mee. Daardoor begrijpt het programma jouw werkwijze beter en kan het jou consistenter en beter ondersteunen. De AI voert geen autonome taken uit zoals een AI-agent, maar werkt alleen met jouw input. Waar te beginnen? Het kan ingewikkeld klinken, maar om een assistent te kunnen inrichten hoef je geen ICT- of programmeringskennis te hebben. Vrijwel alle AI-platformen bieden de mogelijkheid om een eigen assistent te bouwen. Hierbij is de start het meest belangrijk: een AI-assistent is namelijk zo slim als de informatie waarmee je hem voedt. items.title: Art for Everyone: How Public Libraries Expand Access
items.raw_text: Introducing children to viewing, creating, and enjoying art at a young age helps them appreciate it throughout their lives. Some children are exposed to various forms of art because it is part of their daily life or because they have easy access to museums and galleries in their community. But in many areas across the country, access to museums and art galleries can be cost prohibitive. That is where the public library comes in! While some museums, including the Smithsonian Institution in Washington, D.C., offer free admission, millions of people across the country do not have easy access to them. According to the 2024 Annual Survey of Museum-Goers from the American Alliance of Museums and Wilkening Consulting, museum admission costs vary widely, from a few dollars to $40–$50 per adult at some institutions. Among U.S. adults who visit museums at least occasionally, cost was the number one barrier to visiting more often. Among frequent museum-goers, younger adults were twice as likely as seniors to be concerned about admission costs. In response to those barriers, and in an effort to enrich and inspire customers of all ages, many library systems have stepped up to provide access to art in a variety of forms. items.title: Secrets of Effective Upskilling
items.raw_text: This is an excerpt from Upskilling for Library Workers: A Guide for Future-Ready Professionals by Ann Medaille (ALA Editions, 2026). With the advent of new technologies and rapid social and economic shifts, library workers’ jobs are being transformed. Compared with a decade ago, library workers now spend more time consulting on complex research tools, teaching digital literacy classes, supporting virtual learning environments, helping users troubleshoot devices, and codesigning projects with community partners. The pace at which library staffers are called upon to learn new skills is accelerating, and workers may struggle to keep up. In addition, automation and artificial intelligence (AI) are altering many aspects of work. In the long run, technological innovations have the potential to increase productivity and lead to more interesting kinds of work, but in the short term, they often cause disruptions that can be difficult for workers to navigate. To address these changes—and manage the anxieties that come along with them—workers need constant support for skill development. While corporations may embrace upskilling to stay competitive, libraries will have to support upskilling to remain relevant. Library leaders are under greater pressure to respond rapidly to changing social and economic conditions and demonstrate that their libraries make a difference in their communities. items.title: Hold the Phone
items.raw_text: Since fall 2024, each school day at Grant High School in Portland, Oregon, has started the same way: Roughly 2,100 students line up to place their phones in gray and green Yondr pouches—the kind live performers use to prevent audience members from recording—as they enter the building. From the morning bell to dismissal, phones are sealed and can be unlocked only with special magnets near the school’s exits as students leave for the day. The high school’s effort to limit phone use on campus has received support from its educators, who say classroom engagement is on the rise, and mixed reviews from students, who dislike being cut off from their devices. But there’s been one unexpected outcome of the policy: More students are spending time in the library, where they’re browsing the collection or hanging out during free periods, says teacher-librarian Paige Battle. “They’re checking out more books, and I feel like that’s been so important in their education,” Battle says. “We’re seeing studies about students, even adults, not having the reading stamina they’ve had in the past, so I’ve been encouraged by this increase.” Roughly six in 10 parents of an 11- or 12-year-old say their child owns a smartphone, according to a 2025 Pew Research Center survey . And as more schools across the country enact phone-free policies—29 states and the District of Columbia have instituted bell-to-bell phone-free policies so far—many school libraries are experiencing a surge in popularity. items.title: Newsmaker: Min Jin Lee
items.raw_text: Min Jin Lee has notched career milestones that few authors reach. Her immigration saga Pachinko was both a National Book Award finalist and a New York Times Top 10 Best Book of 2017, and it was adapted into a television series of the same name for Apple TV. Lee is also a Guggenheim fellow and the first Korean American to hold the role of New York State author laureate. Her latest title, American Hagwon (Cardinal, September), examines the influence of Korean “cram schools” among families in the Korean diaspora. American Libraries spoke with Lee ahead of her appearance at the American Library Association’s 2026 Annual Conference and Exhibition in Chicago. She discussed her new book, the library that shaped her, and her antidote to book bans. What inspired you to focus on the education system as it relates to the movements of a middle-class Korean American family in American Hagwon ? My research process involved all these interviews—I’ve done hundreds of them, probably almost 1,000 at this point—and every single time I talked to somebody, they would mention their education path. It was such an important and controversial subject. I thought, if I had to think about the most important value for Koreans, especially in the diaspora, what would I write about? items.title: Mall Wonder
items.raw_text: After serving its community for nearly 45 years in the same building, Escondido (Calif.) Public Library closed in April 2025 for an $11.6 million renovation. It was important to us, as the city’s lone library, to preserve access during construction. So one month later, our library opened a temporary location in a very different kind of facility: the nearby North County Mall, where services and collections were spread across six storefronts, including a former Abercrombie & Fitch clothing store. Of course, moving a library takes more than a month. Our planning took more than a year and required staff to work under tight deadlines, limited budgets, and high expectations. Here’s how we did it, and what we learned from the process. Choosing a location. It’s essential to consider whether the new location will match, improve upon, or limit access. Retailers and mall operators have already studied traffic patterns, visibility, parking, and nearby amenities. Leverage that knowledge to evaluate access. In our case, the public benefited from a highway and bus stop near the mall, and adjacency to a city park. The arrangement also gave the mall a stable civic tenant and created natural cross-traffic between library patrons and shoppers. The mall was not just available space; it was a location where public access, economic development, and community visibility could overlap. items.title: Dismantling Disinformation
items.raw_text: Library workers are well aware of the effects of book bans and censorship. Propaganda and disinformation are the flipside of the same coin. Understanding the complex relationships among these interrelated processes is more critical than ever, especially as libraries explore possible solutions and responses. The following books show how disinformation can lead to censorship and how censorship can, in turn, allow disinformation to thrive. Book Bans, Disinformation, and Cultural Erasure: The Censor­ship Movement in Libraries, Schools, and Society By Paul T. Jaeger Jaeger situates the current book-banning movement within a larger social and political effort to erase marginalized communities and culture. He provides clear definitions and examples of these processes and goals, including the roles played by technological progress and economic inequity. With accessible references (like the Beatles, Dungeons & Dragons, and Holmes and Watson) and nuanced examinations of McCarthyism, the history of libraries, and the myth of neutrality, this is a recommended read for anyone interested in a more expansive understanding of current First Amendment challenges. items.title: A Sense of Purpose
items.raw_text: When it comes to building resilient and equitable communities, libraries are natural leaders. We provide places where neighbors meet, learn, and support one another; where sustainability education becomes action; and where residents can find year-round climate refuge. When communities are resilient, they are better able to overcome barriers. The Obama Presidential Center (OPC) branch of Chicago Public Library (CPL) is an example of a library that strengthens the social infrastructure that underpins resilience. CPL Commissioner Chris Brown describes the branch as a civic platform for residents, artists, educators, and organizations to cocreate the life of the library and its surrounding public spaces. Though just 5,000 square feet, OPC was designed to spark connection, invite conversation, and inspire activities that encourage ­socialization and enjoyment. The branch partners with such nonprofits as the Art Institute of Chicago, the literary arts group StoryStudio Chicago , and the artist-led alt_Chicago . OPC is a striking example of how libraries do not just serve resilient communities, they help create them. On the Gulf Coast, sustainability is a daily requirement. Lindsay Cronk, dean of Tulane University Libraries in New Orleans, has shared that the library’s partnership with Keep Louisiana Beautiful , a state program, helps connect students, faculty, and staff with opportunities for conservation, beautification, recycling, and environmental action. items.title: Googles AI Mode toont minder en vooral duurdere producten
items.raw_text: Wie via Googles AI Mode naar een product zoekt, krijgt niet alleen veel minder resultaten te zien dan bij een gewone zoekopdracht, maar betaalt voor identieke artikelen ook regelmatig meer. AI Mode is 21,6 procent duurder. Dat blijkt uit nieuw onderzoek van Productrise , een Nederlands analysebedrijf dat zoekresultaten van Google structureel vergelijkt. Ondernemer Hugo Huijer deed 100.000 identieke zoekopdrachten in Search en AI Mode in de maand augustus en komt tot deze verrassende conclusie. Eén productpaar toont in 38 procent van de gevallen een afwijkende prijsstelling, doorgaans in het nadeel van AI Mode. Qua prijsadvies aan de consument is AI een domoor. Er is geen sprake van een spoortje van intelligentie. Huijer tegen Emerce: “Ik kan geen verklaring geven en Google zegt dat het niet zou moeten gebeuren. Toch is het zo. Wat ik kan verzinnen, maar daarvoor heb ik geen bewijsvoering, is dat AI Mode voorrang geeft aan kwaliteit boven kwantiteit. In AI-resultaten amper ruimte voor productaanbevelingen, dus er wordt scherp gekozen.” Wellicht weegt Google achter de schermen factoren als rating van de winkel, verzend- en retoursnelheid en -kosten en voorraadpositie van de betreffende winkel mee. items.title: Consumentenstichting SMC: Snapchat houdt verslavend ontwerp in stand
items.raw_text: Stichting Massaschade & Consument (SMC) heeft vandaag Snap, het bedrijf achter Snapchat, gedagvaard bij de rechtbank Amsterdam vanwege het verslavende ontwerp van de app. Het is voor het eerst dat een Nederlandse rechter over het verslavende ontwerp van sociale apps moet oordelen, na een golf van vergelijkbare zaken in landen als de Verenigde Staten. Snapchat is een berichtenapp die groot werd met foto’s en berichten die na het bekijken vanzelf verdwijnen. Het telt ruim zes miljoen actieve Nederlandse gebruikers en bereikt meer dan 90% van alle 13- tot 24-jarigen. De unieke combinatie van verdwijnende inhoud, zogenoemde streaks en goed getimede meldingen zorgt voor een constante stroom aan app-interacties die de aandacht van gebruikers opeisen. Deze ‘fear of missing out’ werkt volgens de stichting bijzonder effectief. “Verslaving is bij dit soort apps geen bijeffect, maar een verdienmodel”, zegt SMC-voorzitter Lucia Melcherts. “Natuurlijk is Snapchat óók een makkelijke en leuke manier om dagelijks contact te houden met vrienden. Snap heeft er alleen een extra laag overheen gebouwd, die beloont wie elke dag iets stuurt, straft wie een dag overslaat, en dat meteen aan je vrienden laat zien. Zo wordt contact een verplichting met een teller erop: de vriendschap is misschien echt, maar de streak is iets van Snap.” Snap presenteert Snapchat al jaren als de tegenpool van andere sociale platforms: geen likes en volgers, maar ‘echt contact met echte vrienden’. items.title: Nvidia knuffelt Hugging Face
items.raw_text: Nvidia neemt het ai-bedrijf Hugging Face over voor 12,9 miljard dollar. In het persbericht daarover is symbolisch een hartje geplaatst tussen de ai-chipleverancier en de community van ontwikkelaars die met open modellen werken. Met de strategische acquisitie versnelt de chipgigant zijn inspanningen om het gebruik van open ai-modellen en -diensten te bevorderen. Samen gaan de bedrijven Hugging Face’s platform uitbreiden, de infrastructuur versterken en de toegang voor ontwikkelaars en instituties wereldwijd vergroten. Meer dan achttien miljoen ontwikkelaars, onderzoekers en ‘creators’ gebruiken dit platform. Ze hebben al meer dan drie miljoen modellen, een half miljoen datasets en een miljoen applicaties gedeeld. De zogenoemde open-weightmodellen van Hugging Face vormen een directe uitdaging voor de gesloten, propriëtaire modellen van Amerikaanse techgiganten zoals OpenAI en Anthropic, maar ook voor goedkope Chinese alternatieven. In tegenstelling tot de duurdere gesloten software zoals die van OpenAI en Anthropic zijn open-weight ai-modellen volledig openbaar. Gebruikers kunnen deze modellen downloaden, finetunen en op hun eigen hardware of servers van derden draaien. Ze mogen de getrainde parameters (de gewichten) lokaal kopiëren en wijzigen. Ecosysteem Nvidia-topman Jensen Huang belooft dat Hugging Face een open platform zal blijven voor het hele ai-ecosysteem dat toegang biedt tot dit soort modellen. ‘Open weights verbreden de toegang tot ai en helpen ervoor te zorgen dat

items.title: ChatGPT-advertenties leveren nog weinig op
items.raw_text: Veel mediabureaus zien niet de resultaten die ze verwachten van advertentiecampagnes op ChatGPT. Dat gebeurt ondanks de verbeteringen die OpenAI zegt te hebben doorgevoerd om doelgroepen beter te kunnen bereiken. Peter Jaffray, managing director en privacy officer bij het Canadese digitale marketingbureau Choice OMG, vertelde aan MediaPost dat hij een kleinschalige campagne had uitgevoerd gericht op gebruikers in Ontario en Alberta. De campagne leverde geen enkele geïnteresseerde koper op. Volgens Jaffray waren de advertenties wel daadwerkelijk vertoond en waren de kosten laag. De advertenties bereiken momenteel alleen gebruikers van de gratis versie van ChatGPT, aldus Jaffray. Hij besteedde in totaal 415 dollar aan drie campagnes. OpenAI begon pas in augustus 2026 met het aanbieden van mogelijkheden voor geografische targeting en aangepaste doelgroepen. Tegelijkertijd introduceerde het bedrijf functies voor conversie-optimalisatie, de OpenAI Pixel Conversions API en metingen door externe partijen. Ook Nicholas Verity, CEO van B2B-leadgeneratiebureau Cleverly, testte onlangs advertenties op ChatGPT, maar is daarmee opgehouden. Net als Jaffray zag hij redelijke click-throughpercentages, maar geen enkele conversie. Volgens Verity kwamen de cijfers niet overeen met de werkelijkheid. Hij stelde dat er mogelijk iets mis is met de meetgegevens of dat klikken van dezelfde gebruiker dubbel worden geteld. Daardoor zag hij geen reden om meer geld in de campagnes te steken. items.raw_text: German company Isar Aerospace has successfully launched Europe's first entirely commercial orbital rocket .
